questions.stem: During a conversation, a distressed client becomes tearful and silent after describing a recent loss. Which nursing response best demonstrates active, therapeutic listening?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Fill the silence by giving advice about coping strategies so the client does not become more uncomfortable or feel pressured to continue talking.","B":"Remain present, allow the silence, and then use an open-ended or reflective statement that invites the client to continue at their own pace.","C":"Ask a series of specific yes-or-no questions to keep the discussion efficient and prevent the client from becoming overwhelmed by emotion.","D":"Change to a neutral topic until the client stops crying because discussing the loss while visibly distressed can reinforce emotional dependence."}}
questions.rationale: Therapeutic listening includes remaining present, tolerating silence, reflecting what was heard, and using open-ended prompts rather than rushing into advice, interrogation, or topic change.
questions.source_name: SAMHSA — How to Talk to Someone About Help for Mental Health & Substance Use
questions.source_detail: SAMHSA advises listening carefully, showing that you are listening, reflecting what the person says, and asking open-ended questions.

qc.qc_note: Strict Wave-6 anti-cue rule: max/min option-character ratio <=1.15; correct option is neither unique shortest nor unique longest; distractors manually reviewed for clinical plausibility and wording cues.
